findings.description: `debt.service.ts` exports `GateDebtMeasurement` and `DebtVerdict` interfaces inline, violating the documented rule that exported types live in `*.types.ts` files.
findings.body:
`debt.service.ts` is a new `*.service.ts` file that declares two `export interface`s directly in it: `GateDebtMeasurement` (lines 158-171) and `DebtVerdict` (lines 173-185).

`docs/conventions/general.md` §Type separation states: "Exported types live in `*.types.ts` under the area's `types/` folder — `src/core/types/`, `src/adapters/types/`. **Never inline an exported `type`/`interface` in a `*.service.ts` or `*.routes.ts` file** — the spot-check hook warns on this. Re-export from the consumer if you want a stable call-site path."

This is not aspirational: `.claude/spot-checks.tsv` carries a regex (`\.(service|routes)\.tsx?$` / `^[[:space:]]*export[[:space:]]+(interface|type)[[:space:]]`) run by `.claude/hooks/convention-spot-check.sh` on Stop, which matches both lines verbatim.

Move `GateDebtMeasurement` and `DebtVerdict` into `src/core/types/merge-gate.types.ts` (or a new `debt.types.ts`), and re-export from `debt.service.ts` if a stable `./debt.service.js` import path is wanted for callers such as `debt.test.ts` and `merge-gate.service.ts`.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/31b1681fe0a12edee1e245187ce2d7dc21336069/src/core/debt.service.ts#L158-L185>

findings.description: The new call-site comment on `detectAdapters(repoPath)` restates the JSDoc already on `MergeRequest.adapters` in `src/core/types/merge-gate.types.ts:39-44`; per the seam-duplication rule in `docs/conventions/general.md` §Comments, the call-site copy should be deleted since the field's own doc already carries the WHY.

`gapAside` is a one-liner with a single caller (`judgeDeadCode`); inlining `${gaps.length === 0 ? '' : `; ${gapList(gaps)}`}` at that call site would remove a layer of indirection without loss of clarity, though the name does carry some meaning.

The `judgeDebt` call site builds a `GateDebtMeasurement` inline via spread plus several conditional spreads; a named local variable would let each field read as one concept instead of three levels of conditional spread, though the project uses this idiom elsewhere (e.g. `runMergeGate:331-332`).

The 'Coverage stays one adapter's too' paragraph and the following 'So the coverage gap this decision does not close' paragraph both restate 'one ratio per repo, from the first adapter' — each carries some distinct payload (design rationale vs. the resulting gap), so this is minor overlap rather than a clear duplicate.

The doc comment on `withNote` ("Appends the nested-package note to a detail that exclusion shapes.") restates the function's name and one-line body verbatim, adding no WHY; a competent reader loses nothing if it's deleted.
The doc comment on `gapList` ("`<adapter> not measured — <reason>`, one per gap.") merely echoes the template string built two lines below; the function is self-evident without it.

The doc comment on `samples` ("`a, b, c, …` — the first few of a list, the rest elided.") restates the one-line slice+join+ellipsis body directly below it, adding no WHY (e.g. no mention of why `DEBT_DETAIL_SAMPLES` was picked).

Nearly every test case that pairs with a documented branch in `debt.service.ts` repeats that branch's inline WHY comment almost verbatim (recurring ~8-10 times) rather than stating a test-specific fact — this is stale-risk duplication that will drift if one side is edited and not the other, even though each individual comment is accurate.

`sanitizeReason(g.adapterId)` guards a value that in practice is always a compile-time literal or content from the protected `.pupitre/adapter.yml` path, never session-controlled worktree content — defensive layering rather than a reachable attack surface, but harmless to keep.

`measureDebt` has no collision check on adapter `id` when building `gaps`; an operator-authored `.pupitre/adapter.yml` reusing a built-in id like `python` would produce an ambiguous joined gap report (e.g. "python: X; python: Y"). Only reachable via a protected, operator-controlled path, not by a session, so this is a usability nit rather than a security issue.
